front.title: Signed Custody Receipts Carried in a Bundle Protocol Version 7 Extension Block

abstract.t: This document defines the Custody Receipt Block, a Bundle Protocol Version 7 (BPv7) extension block that carries a chain of signed custody receipts inside the bundle those receipts describe. Each node that chooses to act as a custodian appends one receipt stating that it held the bundle, which node it received it from, and when it received and forwarded it. Nodes that do not implement the block forward it unchanged and are never required to read the payload or to sign anything. A verifier holding the custodians' public keys can check the chain after the fact and can report, rather than infer, any part of the route for which no receipt exists. The receipts are evidence for accounting and dispute resolution between operators. They are not Bundle Protocol administrative records and they do not replace or modify custody transfer signalling.

note.name: About This Document
note.t: An open reference implementation (Apache-2.0), test vectors and live interoperability results are at . The implementation uses block type 224 from the private and experimental range pending any assignment.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: In a delay/disruption tolerant network, a bundle may be held for minutes to hours by nodes run by different operators before it reaches its destination. When something goes wrong (a bundle arrives late, is lost, or arrives altered), each operator holds only its own local logs. Those logs are not portable evidence: another party cannot verify them without trusting the operator that wrote them.

BPv7 does not include custody transfer; reliable hop-by-hop transfer is addressed separately . Custody transfer answers "who is responsible for retransmission now". This document addresses a different question: "who can prove they held this bundle, and when". The mechanism is a signed receipt that travels with the bundle and can be verified by any party, at any later time, without contacting the nodes that produced it.

The design follows the end-to-end argument : forwarding nodes do nothing beyond normal BPv7 block processing. Only nodes whose operators choose to act as custodians produce receipts, and no node parses the payload: a custodian hashes the bytes it holds. A verifier at the destination, or any later auditor, does the checking.

This document is published as Experimental so that the format can be evaluated in multi-operator deployments. This revision defines version 2 receipts, a CBOR payload signed as a COSE_Sign1 and bound to the BPv7 bundle identity; the version 1 encoding of revision -00 is kept in so that receipts already produced remain verifiable. Both have been run through five BPv7 paths built from four independent implementations; see .

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: A node whose operator has chosen to sign receipts for bundles it holds. Being a custodian in this sense is independent of custody transfer and implies no retransmission responsibility.
Any BPv7 node that is not acting as a custodian for a given bundle. A forwarder may or may not implement this specification.
The first custodian for a bundle.
A signed statement by one custodian that it held one bundle, defined in . A receipt is not a BPv7 administrative record ().
The ordered list of receipts carried in one Custody Receipt Block.
A part of the route, visible to a verifier, for which no receipt exists.

section.name: Custody Receipt Format
section.t: A version 2 custody receipt is a COSE_Sign1 structure (), untagged, whose payload is a CBOR map signed by one custodian.

section.name: Signature
section.t: The protected header MUST contain the algorithm parameter (label 1). Implementations MUST support EdDSA (value -8) with Ed25519 (, ). The unprotected header map is empty in this version, and no external additional authenticated data is used. The signing key is identified by the custodian EID in the payload; key distribution is out of scope ().

section.name: Payload

tr.td: EID of the node the custodian received the bundle from
Bundle identity of what was held ()
SHA-256 of the payload block's block-type-specific data as held

section.sourcecode: custody-receipt = COSE_Sign1 ; RFC 9052, untagged receipt-payload = { 1 => eid-text, ; prevHop 2 => eid-text, ; thisHop 3 => bundle-identity, 4 => bstr .size 32, ; payloadHash, SHA-256 5 => uint, ; receivedAt, DTN time 6 => uint, ; forwardedAt, DTN time ? 7 => tstr, ; subject } bundle-identity = [ eid-text, [ uint, uint ] ] ; whole bundle / [ eid-text, [ uint, uint ], uint, uint ] ; fragment eid-text = tstr ; EID in text form
section.t: A custodian SHOULD take prevHop from the Previous Node block () when one is present. An encoded receipt is about 156 octets.

section.name: Bundle Identity and Payload Binding
section.t: The bundle identity is the source node ID and creation timestamp of the bundle and, when the custodian holds a fragment, the fragment offset and total application data unit length, all taken from the primary block (). A custodian computes payloadHash over the payload block's block-type-specific data without interpreting it. No custodian parses the application data unit, including the first one, and the binding holds when the payload is encrypted by a Block Confidentiality Block , since the custodian hashes the ciphertext it holds.
Any verifier can check the binding with no application knowledge. An application that needs its own identifier MAY carry it in subject; verifiers that do not know the application ignore it.

section.name: Fragments
section.t: The block is replicated in every fragment (). A receipt made before fragmentation names the whole bundle and therefore covers every fragment, but its payloadHash can only be checked after reassembly. A custodian that holds a fragment signs for that fragment: its bundle identity includes the fragment offset and total length, and its payloadHash covers that fragment's payload. A receipt naming a different fragment of the same bundle does not cover the fragment it is found in.

section.name: Block Format
section.t: The block-type code is TBD1 (). Implementations of this version use 224, from the private and experimental range, until a code point is assigned.

The block-type-specific data is a CBOR array of receipts in the order they were appended. In version 2 each element is a COSE_Sign1 array; in version 1 () each element is a text string. A block MUST hold receipts of one version only.
A bundle MUST NOT contain more than one Custody Receipt Block.

section.name: Block Processing Control Flags
section.t: The block MUST have "Block must be replicated in every fragment" set, and MUST have "Delete bundle if block can't be processed" and "Discard block if it can't be processed" clear. A node that does not implement this specification therefore retains the block and forwards it unchanged (). A CRC-32C is RECOMMENDED.

section.name: Custodian Behavior
section.t: A custodian that holds a bundle and chooses to sign for it derives the bundle identity and payloadHash from what it holds, signs a receipt, appends it to the array (adding the block if absent) and recomputes the block CRC. It MUST NOT alter or reorder earlier receipts, and MUST NOT append a version 2 receipt to a block of version 1 receipts.
Which bundles a node signs for is local policy (for example, by source, destination, service agreement or the presence of the block). No new naming scheme is needed.

section.name: Forwarder Behavior
section.t: A forwarder performs normal BPv7 processing. It does not read the payload, does not sign, and need not implement this specification.

section.name: Verification
section.t: For each receipt, a verifier: verifies the COSE_Sign1 under a key it obtained independently for the EID in thisHop (failure: signature_invalid, or custodian_not_pinned when it has no key); checks that bundle equals the identity of the bundle received or, when the received bundle is a fragment, the identity of the whole bundle (failure: wrong_bundle); and, when bundle equals the identity received, checks payloadHash against the payload received (failure: payload_hash_mismatch). A whole-bundle receipt found in a fragment is reported as not hash-checked.
Two modes are defined:

dl.dd: The verifier knows the expected ordered list of custodians. The number of receipts MUST equal the length of the list, each thisHop MUST match its position, and each prevHop after the first MUST equal the previous receipt's thisHop.

The verifier knows the custodians' keys but not the route. Wherever a receipt's prevHop differs from the previous receipt's thisHop (or from the expected origin), and wherever the node that delivered the bundle (from its Previous Node block) differs from the last receipt's thisHop, the verifier MUST report a gap naming the last signed hop, the next signed hop, and the unsigned node observed. A result with any gap MUST NOT be reported as complete. Because each node replaces the Previous Node block, a gap names at least one unsigned node, not necessarily all of them.

section.t: A missing receipt is reported as missing and is never inferred. A receipt that is present but invalid is a failure, not a gap. A verifier SHOULD bound the number of receipts it processes.

section.name: Interaction with BPSec
section.t: Because every custodian modifies the Custody Receipt Block, a Block Integrity Block MUST NOT target it. Receipts carry their own signatures. A BIB that targets the payload or the primary block is unaffected by appending receipts, since appending changes neither. A Block Confidentiality Block MUST NOT target the Custody Receipt Block, because every custodian appends to it.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: Note to the RFC Editor: please remove this section before publication, as described in .

One implementation exists: dtn-custody-demo, Embryo Space Inc., Apache-2.0, JavaScript (Node.js) with no third-party dependencies, . It includes its own BPv7 codec, checked byte for byte against the uD3TN project's Python library, and implements both receipt versions. In live runs the block, with version 1 or version 2 receipts and with a payload BIB beside it, was carried byte-identical across a scheduled contact gap by uD3TN, NASA HDTN, JPL ION and Aalyria Hardy, and along one path through uD3TN and then NASA HDTN; none of them implement it. The audit mode reported the unsigned stretch through each stack that adds a Previous Node block. uD3TN adds one only when built with a compile-time option that is off by default; with it enabled, the uD3TN path was reported the same way. Deployments that rely on the audit need forwarders that emit Previous Node blocks. Results and commands are in the repository (transport/bpv7/RESULTS.md).

Testing against JPL ION as a BIB acceptor and signer found that ION builds the integrity-protected plaintext for a payload target from the whole serialized block rather than from the block-type-specific data as a byte string (), and omits the SHA variant parameter while signing with HMAC 256/256. This has been reported to the ION maintainers. The reference implementation interoperates with ION through an optional mode and uses the RFC 9173 construction by default.

ul.li: Key identification. Keys are found by thisHop. A COSE key identifier (kid) would allow key rotation without changing EIDs.

Batching. The block grows by one receipt per custodian. A custodian could instead sign one receipt per contact over a Merkle root of the bundles it held, as the reference implementation does outside the block; how such a receipt is carried in each bundle is not yet specified.
Other signature algorithms. Only EdDSA is required. Whether to require a second algorithm (for example ES256) for flight hardware with existing cryptographic support is open.
Reassembly. A verifier that reassembles fragments could check whole-bundle receipts against the reassembled payload; the procedure is not yet specified.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Key distribution. Receipts are only as meaningful as the binding between a custodian EID and its key. Verifiers MUST obtain keys independently of the receipts and MUST NOT trust a key carried with a receipt.

Stripping. Any forwarder can remove the block or truncate the array and recompute the CRC. This cannot be prevented by the block itself; it is detected because the removed custodians appear as gaps. A verifier MUST treat a gap as absence of evidence, not as evidence of absence.
Replay. A receipt copied to another bundle fails verification because it names the bundle identity and payload hash of what was held.

False times. A custodian can sign false receivedAt and forwardedAt values. Receipts bind a custodian to its claims; they do not prove the claims are true. Inconsistent times across adjacent receipts can be flagged by the verifier.
Denial of service. Verification cost and block size grow linearly with the number of receipts. A verifier SHOULD bound the number of receipts it will process.
Privacy. Receipts reveal the custodians on a route and their timing to anyone who can read the bundle.

section.t: IANA is requested to assign one value (TBD1) in the "Bundle Block Types" registry of the "Bundle Protocol" registry group:

section.name: Version 1 Receipts
section.t: Revision -00 of this document defined version 1 receipts, which remain in use. A version 1 receipt is a JSON object carried in the block as its canonical form (keys sorted recursively by UTF-16 code unit, no insignificant whitespace). Its members are kind ("custody/1"), payloadId, bundleId, prevHop, thisHop, receivedAt and forwardedAt (milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z), claimId ("0x" and the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the canonical form without claimId, sig and signerPub), sig (base64 Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 bytes of claimId) and signerPub (base64 DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo ). The origin sets payloadId and bundleId from the application data unit; later custodians copy them from the first receipt. An encoded version 1 receipt is about 530 octets.

ul.li: Version 2 receipts: a CBOR payload signed as COSE_Sign1 (EdDSA), about 156 octets instead of about 530. Version 1 moved to .
Receipts are bound to the BPv7 bundle identity and a hash of the payload bytes held, so no custodian parses the payload and any verifier can check the binding.
Implementation status updated: a path through two implementations, version 2 receipts live, and the JPL ION BPSec report.
